name: dwarf
why: An object file manipulation tool that opens the door to ELF and DWARF debug structures.

brief.what_it_is: dwarf-ng is a command-line object file manipulation tool and hex editor, described as being in the spirit of gdb. It opens raw files and ELF (32 and 64-bit), PE (PE32 and PE+), and Mach-O (macOS 32 and 64-bit) executables, and lets you read and edit section headers and raw data. It can also create new file headers, inject headers and code or data into a file, and be used as a compiler back-end to produce executables or object files. Input is a file; output is printed hex, strings, numbers, and edited or saved files.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a little but powerful tool for reading and editing object files at the header and raw-byte level, the way gdb works on a running program, and for building or patching binaries directly.
brief.how_it_works: You open a file (probed for its type, or opened raw with oO) and get a shell-like prompt where commands follow a gdb-like syntax: a letter for the operation, optional ? for help, and arguments such as an address or block size. Format-specific structures are exposed as variables such as $elf, $ph[0..n], $sh[0..n] for ELF, $mac and $lc for Mach-O, and $pe and $sect for PE, which can be printed, assigned, and used in expressions. Config files /etc/dwarfrc and ~/.dwarfrc are read in that order, and a work_on_tmpcopy option controls whether edits go to a temporary copy.

brief.install_notes: Build from source with make; on macOS pass FLEX=osx. Dependencies listed in the README are flex, bison, readline (libreadline and libreadline-dev on Linux), and gcc. Install with sudo make install. Optional configuration lives in /etc/dwarfrc and ~/.dwarfrc, with settings such as work_on_tmpcopy, verbose, tmpdir, tmpname, and colors. No accounts or hardware are needed.
brief.standout: It is a gdb-style hex editor that understands several executable formats at once and exposes their headers as scriptable variables that you can assign, resize, and rebuild, including adding new program or section headers. The README also pitches it as a compiler back-end.
brief.status: Unknown from the README alone. The help banner reads dwarf-ng-0.4.0 with copyright 2007-2013-2017, and the README has no release dates, changelog, or recent-activity note. I did not check the repository's commit history or releases page.
brief.caveats: The README says Raw, ELF, PE, and Mach-O are the only formats handled now and that new types will come later. Build needs flex, bison, readline, and gcc, and macOS needs the FLEX=osx flag. The README does not describe parsing DWARF debug information, so the name refers to the tool's 'dwarf' identity and not obviously to the DWARF debug format; the scout note's link to DWARF debug structures is not supported by the README text. Licence is GPL v2 or later. The docs are a man page link and a short example set, and the README does not say how to test changes.
quotes: a little and powerful object file manipulation tool and hex editor.
in the spirit of _gdb_. with dwarf-ng you can read and edit all the file's section headers as well as the raw data.
it can be used as a compiler back-end to create executables/object files.
